## Overview

`statarbor` provides an end-to-end, assumption-guided statistical workflow for
experimental datasets in agriculture, plant biotechnology, and life sciences.
Rather than requiring users to manually run assumption diagnostics, select
matching post-hoc procedures, construct compact letter displays (CLD), and
format manuscript tables separately, `statarbor` unifies these steps into a
transparent, reproducible R package and bilingual (English/Turkish) Shiny
interface.

### Automated Decision Tree

For independent multi-group numeric comparisons, `auto_compare()` applies the
following routing hierarchy at significance threshold $\alpha$:

| Diagnostic Condition | Routed Hypothesis Test | Post-Hoc Procedure | Effect Size |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Any group with zero variance ($s^2 = 0$) | Kruskal-Wallis | Dunn (Bonferroni / Holm / BH) | $\varepsilon^2$ |
| Shapiro-Wilk normality violated ($p < \alpha$) | Kruskal-Wallis | Dunn (Bonferroni / Holm / BH) | $\varepsilon^2$ |
| Normal, but Levene homogeneity violated ($p < \alpha$) | Welch one-way ANOVA | Games-Howell (native) | Estimated $\omega^2$ |
| Normality and homogeneity both satisfied | One-way ANOVA | Tukey HSD | $\eta^2$, $\omega^2$ |

## 1. Benchmark Dataset (`thermal_stress`)

`statarbor` ships with a synthetic 120-observation thermal stress dataset
(`thermal_stress`) engineered to exercise all statistical pathways simultaneously:

```{r load-data}
library(statarbor)
data(thermal_stress)
str(thermal_stress)
```

## 2. Automated Group Comparisons & Special-Character-Safe CLD

Running `auto_compare()` on three distinct traits automatically triggers all
three decision pathways:

```{r auto-compare}
res_emb <- auto_compare(thermal_stress, response = "embryo_mm", group = "treatment")
res_fw  <- auto_compare(thermal_stress, response = "fresh_weight_g", group = "treatment")
res_sh  <- auto_compare(thermal_stress, response = "shoot_cm", group = "treatment")

print(res_emb)
print(res_fw)
print(res_sh)
```

## 3. Numerical Cross-Validation Against Base R Reference Implementations

To verify computational accuracy, the table below compares `statarbor` test
statistics and p-values directly against base R (`stats::aov()`,
`stats::oneway.test()`, `stats::kruskal.test()`):

```{r cross-validation}
ref_aov <- stats::anova(stats::aov(embryo_mm ~ treatment, data = thermal_stress))
ref_w   <- stats::oneway.test(fresh_weight_g ~ treatment, data = thermal_stress, var.equal = FALSE)
ref_kw  <- stats::kruskal.test(shoot_cm ~ treatment, data = thermal_stress)

val_tbl <- data.frame(
  Response = c("embryo_mm", "fresh_weight_g", "shoot_cm"),
  Routed_Method = c(res_emb$method, res_fw$method, res_sh$method),
  statarbor_Stat = round(c(res_emb$statistic, res_fw$statistic, res_sh$statistic), 6),
  BaseR_Stat = round(c(ref_aov$`F value`[1], as.numeric(ref_w$statistic), as.numeric(ref_kw$statistic)), 6),
  Max_Abs_Diff_Stat = signif(abs(c(
    res_emb$statistic - ref_aov$`F value`[1],
    res_fw$statistic - as.numeric(ref_w$statistic),
    res_sh$statistic - as.numeric(ref_kw$statistic)
  )), 3),
  statarbor_p = signif(c(res_emb$p_value, res_fw$p_value, res_sh$p_value), 6),
  BaseR_p = signif(c(ref_aov$`Pr(>F)`[1], as.numeric(ref_w$p.value), as.numeric(ref_kw$p.value)), 6),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(val_tbl, caption = "Numerical Cross-Validation: statarbor vs. Base R Reference Functions")
```

## 4. Cleaning Raw Experimental Spreadsheets

Raw laboratory files often label control replicates individually (e.g.,
`"Control 1"`, `"Control 2"`, ..., `"Control 63"`) or store factorial levels in
separate columns. `merge_group_prefix()` and `combine_factors()` standardize
these columns cleanly:

```{r data-prep}
raw_lab <- data.frame(
  grp = c("Control 1", "Control 2", "Control 3", "+4C - 1W", "+4C - 1W"),
  temp = c("Ctrl", "Ctrl", "Ctrl", "4C", "4C"),
  week = c("0W", "0W", "0W", "1W", "1W"),
  shoot = c(10.5, 11.2, 9.8, 7.6, 6.9),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

clean_lab <- merge_group_prefix(raw_lab, column = "grp", prefix = "Control")
clean_lab <- combine_factors(clean_lab, cols = c("temp", "week"), sep = " - ")
clean_lab
```

## 5. Publication-Ready CLD Figures

```{r plots, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
plot(res_fw, type = "boxplot")
plot(res_sh, type = "violin")
```

## 6. Advanced Modeling: Binary Separation (Firth), Ordinal CLM, and Factorial GLM

```{r advanced}
# 1. Two-group ploidy comparison (auto-routed t-test or Mann-Whitney U)
compare_two_groups(thermal_stress, response = "shoot_cm", group = "ploidy")

# 2. Binary germination with complete separation (100% Control, 0% -20C_1W)
analyze_binary(thermal_stress, response = "germination", group = "treatment")

# 3. Factorial Gamma-log GLM on strictly positive fresh weight
analyze_interaction(
  thermal_stress,
  response = "fresh_weight_g",
  factors = c("temperature_c", "ploidy"),
  family = "gamma_log"
)
```

```{r ordinal, eval = requireNamespace("ordinal", quietly = TRUE)}
# 4. Ordered tissue viability score (0-3) via Cumulative Link Model
analyze_ordinal(thermal_stress, response = "viability_score", group = "treatment")
```

## 7. Experimental Designs (`v0.2.0`)

Version `0.2.0` expands `statarbor` beyond independent one-way comparisons to
cover five core experimental designs, each with assumption diagnostics,
special-character-safe CLD, S3 `plot()` support, bilingual methods reporting,
and executable verification scripts.

### 7.1 Paired and Repeated-Measures Designs

```{r repeated-designs}
set.seed(42)
n_subj <- 12
subj_eff <- stats::rnorm(n_subj, 0, 1.5)

# Paired 2-condition comparison (paired t-test vs. Wilcoxon signed-rank)
paired_df <- data.frame(
  plant_id = rep(paste0("P", seq_len(n_subj)), 2),
  stage = factor(rep(c("Pre-Stress", "Post-Stress"), each = n_subj),
                 levels = c("Pre-Stress", "Post-Stress")),
  chlorophyll = c(12 + subj_eff + stats::rnorm(n_subj, 0, 0.7),
                  9.5 + subj_eff + stats::rnorm(n_subj, 0, 0.7))
)
res_paired <- compare_paired(paired_df, response = "chlorophyll",
                             condition = "stage", id = "plant_id")
print(res_paired)

# Repeated-measures comparison (k >= 3, Greenhouse-Geisser RM-ANOVA vs. Friedman)
rep_df <- data.frame(
  plant_id = factor(rep(paste0("P", seq_len(n_subj)), 3)),
  timepoint = factor(rep(c("Week 1", "Week 2", "Week 3"), each = n_subj),
                     levels = c("Week 1", "Week 2", "Week 3")),
  shoot_cm = c(8 + subj_eff + stats::rnorm(n_subj, 0, 0.6),
               11 + subj_eff + stats::rnorm(n_subj, 0, 0.6),
               15 + subj_eff + stats::rnorm(n_subj, 0, 0.6))
)
res_rep <- auto_repeated(rep_df, response = "shoot_cm",
                         condition = "timepoint", id = "plant_id")
print(res_rep)
```

### 7.2 Count Data Regression (`analyze_count()`)

`analyze_count()` screens Pearson overdispersion on a baseline Poisson GLM and
routes automatically to Negative Binomial (`MASS::glm.nb`, with Quasi-Poisson
fallback). Groups with all-zero counts are evaluated via two-group
likelihood-ratio tests to avoid Hauck-Donner Wald distortion:

```{r count-design}
set.seed(101)
n_c <- 18
count_df <- data.frame(
  treatment = factor(rep(c("Control", "+4C - 1W", "-20C - Lethal"), each = n_c),
                     levels = c("Control", "+4C - 1W", "-20C - Lethal")),
  leaf_count = c(stats::rnbinom(n_c, mu = 10, size = 1.8),
                 stats::rnbinom(n_c, mu = 4, size = 1.8),
                 rep(0L, n_c))
)
res_cnt <- analyze_count(count_df, response = "leaf_count", group = "treatment")
print(res_cnt)
```

### 7.3 Analysis of Covariance (`analyze_ancova()`)

`analyze_ancova()` verifies homogeneity of regression slopes before computing
Type II sums of squares and covariate-adjusted marginal means:

```{r ancova-design}
set.seed(202)
init_mm <- stats::rnorm(45, mean = 5, sd = 1)
ancova_df <- data.frame(
  treatment = factor(rep(c("Control", "Primed - Low", "Primed - High"), each = 15),
                     levels = c("Control", "Primed - Low", "Primed - High")),
  initial_mm = init_mm,
  final_cm = 4 + 1.5 * init_mm + rep(c(0, 2.5, 5.2), each = 15) + stats::rnorm(45, 0, 0.9)
)
res_anc <- analyze_ancova(ancova_df, response = "final_cm",
                          group = "treatment", covariate = "initial_mm")
print(res_anc)
```

### 7.4 Randomized Complete Block Design (`analyze_rcbd()`)

`analyze_rcbd()` evaluates fixed (or optional `lme4` random) block designs,
reporting Cochran-Cox relative efficiency of blocking alongside Tukey-Kramer
pairwise comparisons and CLD:

```{r rcbd-design}
set.seed(303)
rcbd_df <- expand.grid(
  treatment = c("Control", "Bio-Fert A", "Bio-Fert B", "NPK Std"),
  block = paste0("Block_", 1:5),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
rcbd_df$treatment <- factor(rcbd_df$treatment,
                            levels = c("Control", "Bio-Fert A", "Bio-Fert B", "NPK Std"))
rcbd_df$block <- factor(rcbd_df$block)
blk_eff <- stats::setNames(c(-2.5, -1.2, 0, 1.3, 2.4), levels(rcbd_df$block))
trt_eff <- stats::setNames(c(18, 22, 27, 31), levels(rcbd_df$treatment))
rcbd_df$yield_kg <- trt_eff[as.character(rcbd_df$treatment)] +
  blk_eff[as.character(rcbd_df$block)] + stats::rnorm(nrow(rcbd_df), 0, 0.9)

res_rcbd <- analyze_rcbd(rcbd_df, response = "yield_kg",
                         treatment = "treatment", block = "block")
print(res_rcbd)
```

```{r rcbd-plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
plot(res_rcbd)
```

## 8. Reproducible Methods Text, R Script Export, and Interactive Interface

All `auto_compare()`, `compare_paired()`, `auto_repeated()`, `analyze_count()`,
`analyze_ancova()`, and `analyze_rcbd()` objects generate manuscript-ready
English or Turkish methods text and self-contained verification scripts:

```{r reporting}
cat(generate_methods_text(res_rcbd, lang = "en"), "\n\n")
cat(generate_methods_text(res_rcbd, lang = "tr"), "\n")
```

```{r script-export}
script_lines <- export_r_script(res_rcbd, data_name = "rcbd_df")
cat(utils::head(script_lines, 18), sep = "\n")
```

To launch the interactive bilingual (English/Turkish) Shiny web application
locally with zero coding required:

```r
statarbor::run_app()
```
